title: Distilling Instructions into Weights: Closed-Form Edits Fix a Robot Policy's Misreading
why_wsp: A Claude Opus operator session (and seven blind Claude Opus editors) edit a pi0.5 VLA policy's weights with closed-form, gradient-free updates computed from activations, chiefly a multi-key minimum-norm update that writes the effect of a known-good instruction rewording into VLM MLP weights.
domain: robot manipulation (vision-language-action policy, RoboLab in Isaac Sim)
editor: Claude Opus (operator session and seven blind autonomous editors); GPT-6 Astra edits from companion study; released tool 'weightsmith distill' computes the closed form
target: OpenPI pi0.5 DROID checkpoint, 'about 3.35 billion parameters' (Sec. 3)
interface: closed form (regularized minimum-norm multi-key update, Eq. 1) built in a NumPy sandbox with activation capture
loop: closed-loop with feedback (offline replay check, practice-seed closed-loop eval, then frozen for held-out)
self_editing: no; Claude Opus edits a separate robot policy
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: 'The full edit is low-rank but not sparse. It changes 13.4% of the policy's stored values, and the 0.16% variant still changes 7.4% once applied.' (Sec. 5); low-rank factors of the small variant are '5.3 million parameters, or 0.16% of the parameter count' (Sec. 4.2)

headline_results.quote: success rises from 27/128 (21.1%) to 106/128 (82.8%), with 81 episodes fixed and 2 broken

headline_results.claim: Random-direction control of same size does nothing
headline_results.quote: a random-direction update with the same layers, rank, and singular values scored 9/64
this variant scores 102/128 against 19/128 (86 fixed, 3 broken; exact p = 3.8 × 10−22 )
picking up the eyeglasses rises from 22/64 to 44/64

headline_results.claim: Released tool reproduces fix end to end
headline_results.quote: Success rose from 8/64 to 36/64, with 33 starts fixed and 5 broken

headline_results.claim: Only 1 of 7 blind Claude Opus editors passed held-out

headline_results.quote: Edits at the other failure levels did not help (Fig. 3).

cost.quote: The budget was 96 practice episodes and 192 activation items.

baselines_and_controls: unedited policy on paired seeds; random-direction update of identical layers/rank/singular values; explicit rewording with unchanged weights; alternative edit locations (action expert, action head); unedited and identically-edited reruns as noise controls; Holm correction over seven blind editors
runs_and_variance: Paired seeds with exact McNemar, bootstrap (20,000 draws) and Wilson intervals; noise floor measured: 'rerunning unchanged weights flips about a third of paired outcomes' (Abstract); 'The unedited policy scored 14/16 and then 8/16 on the same 16 butter seeds.' (Sec. 4.8)
robustness_of_edits: Distribution shift across tasks tested: transfers to 2 tasks, no significant harm on remaining 13 ('all exact p ≥ 0.12'); cube-right-of-bowl stays 0/32. No fine-tuning or quantization tests.
verification: statistical only (paired held-out seeds, exact McNemar, Wilson/bootstrap intervals, pre-registration for edit-location study)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Blind editor independently traced cube-then-banana failure to wording and wrote a different (action-head gated) edit; authors conclude edits re-route an existing computation: 'Distillation re-routes a computation the network already performs. It did not create one that is missing.' (Sec. 5)
limitations_stated: Edit is low-rank not sparse; distilled edit built by operator session; tool run on one task and needs a known-good wording; edit-location comparison covers one task and wording; transfer not predicted in advance; one zero-shot checkpoint in simulation; failure levels assigned without independent rater.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab 2026 'Sparks of weight-space programming' blog
Guo and Xie 2026 X thread (robot weight editing)
Gupta et al. 2026 'Can frontier LLMs fix robots by editing their weights?' blog
Abbas and Seraj 2026 companion study (GPT-6 Astra on pi0.5, in weightsmith repo)
MEMIT / ROME (Meng et al.) closed-form multi-key update
notes_for_survey: The working edit is a MEMIT-style closed-form update aimed at a prompt rewording (instruction distillation) rather than free-form LLM weight writing, and it changes 13.4% of stored values. Strong evaluation hygiene: paired seeds, random-direction control, measured noise floor (about a third of pairs flip on reruns). Negative results across perception, missing skill, contact and gripper failures.
